articles.title: NBA star Jalen Brunson brings Thanksgiving cheer to New York, providing nearly 1,000 grocery bags and winter coats to Bronx and East Harlem families
articles.summary: NBA star Jalen Brunson partners with DREAM Charter Schools to provide nearly 1,000 grocery bags and winter coats to families in need ahead of Thanksgiving, helping to ease the holiday burden.
articles.body: Jalen Brunson is used to bringing New York together at Madison Square Garden, but his latest contribution to the city has nothing to do with basketball. The Knicks point guard has joined forces with DREAM Charter Schools for a third consecutive year, helping nearly 500 students and their families prepare for Thanksgiving while ensuring children have winter coats for the colder months. The initiative combines two practical forms of support for households across the Bronx and East Harlem.Jalen Brunson and Second Round Foundation organise Thanksgiving giveawayBrunson's Second Round Foundation partnered with DREAM Charter Schools for the distribution on November 19, 2026, at the DREAM Highbridge Community Room, located at 1162 River Avenue in the Bronx. The event ran from 4pm to 6pm and marked the third consecutive year of the organisations' Thanksgiving partnership.The foundation purchased nearly 1,000 grocery bags containing fresh fruit, vegetables, meat, dry goods and traditional Thanksgiving staples, including stuffing and pies. The packages were intended to help families prepare their holiday meals while easing some of the additional food costs that come with the Thanksgiving period.Brunson's foundation also partnered with nonprofit organisation Operation Warm to provide winter coats for participating students. The clothing distribution addresses another seasonal expense for families as temperatures begin to fall, allowing the initiative to support both household food needs and children's winter clothing.Nearly 500 DREAM students and their households were expected to benefit from the combined giveaway.Brunson previously donated more than $300,000 to DREAM's culinary programmeThe Thanksgiving initiative builds on Brunson's wider involvement with DREAM Charter Schools, which extends beyond the annual holiday distribution. In July 2025, the Knicks guard donated more than $300,000, with reports putting the contribution at $328,000, to support the organisation's Scratch Food Kitchen programme.During a visit to DREAM Charter High School in the Bronx, Brunson also cooked alongside students, helping promote nutritious daily meals and introduce young people to opportunities in the culinary industry. The programme supports food education, culinary career internships and youth empowerment, connecting practical skills with healthier eating habits.His involvement has given the partnership a longer-term focus on student opportunities, alongside the immediate assistance provided through the Thanksgiving and winter coat drive.DREAM Charter Schools supports more than 2,800 young peopleFounded in 1991, DREAM Charter Schools serves more than 2,800 young people through seven schools across East Harlem and the South Bronx. Its programmes include free early childhood education, kindergarten through 12th-grade schooling, year-round enrichment and six years of post-secondary support following high school graduation.The organisation works across several stages of students' development, from early education through the transition to further study and employment. Its partnership with Brunson's foundation adds direct assistance for families to that educational work, particularly during a period when food and clothing expenses can place additional pressure on household budgets.Through the latest distribution, Second Round Foundation and DREAM have continued a three-year effort to provide practical support to the communities they serve, with nearly 1,000 grocery bags and winter coats reaching families ahead of the holiday season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luka Doncic gets a major Kareem Abdul-Jabbar endorsement as Lakers' post-LeBron era takes shape
articles.summary: Lakers legend Kareem Abdul-Jabbar has publicly cleared Luka Doncic to take over the franchise from LeBron James.
articles.body: Lakers legend Kareem Abdul-Jabbar has publicly cleared Luka Doncic to take over the franchise from LeBron James. In a Substack column, Abdul-Jabbar told worried fans to relax after James left for Philadelphia. Los Angeles sits at 13-3 with ten new players, and Doncic leads the NBA at 38.1 points per game through 14 appearances. Teammate Walker Kessler added his own support this week, pushing back on the idea that Doncic is a poor defender. The Lakers’ nine-game winning streak ended with a 109-97 loss to Utah, yet Abdul-Jabbar saw little reason to worry.Why did Kareem Abdul-Jabbar pick Luka Doncic to lead the post-LeBron Lakers?Abdul-Jabbar wrote that few people expected much from the Lakers this year. James had left, ten new players had arrived, and matching last season’s 53 wins looked like a heavy lift, even with Doncic and Austin Reaves back in the backcourt.Los Angeles went 13-3 anyway. After the Jazz ended the streak, Abdul-Jabbar kept his message simple. “Luka has shown he’s more than ready to wear the crown,” he wrote.The praise matters because Abdul-Jabbar picks his spots. He and Magic Johnson built the 1980s Lakers into the league’s top franchise during the rivalry with Boston, and Kobe Bryant, Shaquille O’Neal and James kept the team relevant after them.The pressure on Doncic has only grown. His trade from Dallas stunned the league, and the Slovenian star’s first Los Angeles postseason ended in a first-round loss to Minnesota. Then James, Rui Hachimura and other starters left. Doncic has responded by lifting a reshaped roster to an elite early record.The production backs the praise. Doncic is adding 7.0 rebounds and 7.6 assists to the scoring, and the Lakers are doing it with a roster few people picked to match last year’s 53 wins.Kessler and Redick back Doncic on defenseKessler has heard the criticism and does not buy it. On The Old Man and The Three podcast, the center called Doncic “a better defender than a lot of people think.” He pointed to Doncic’s work in passing lanes and on help-side rotations, and called him very smart.The numbers back Kessler up. The six-time All-Star averages 1.9 steals and 0.6 blocks, and opponents have shot 37.7 percent on attempts he defends. Against Toronto on Nov. 1, Doncic piled up 45 points, 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals and a block in a 131-125 win. It ranks among his most complete games of the year. Coach JJ Redick has also praised Doncic’s positioning, communication, and activity inside the defensive scheme.The MVP award is the next target. Doncic reached the Finals with Kyrie Irving in Dallas but has never come close to the award, and winning it would put him on a list with Abdul-Jabbar, Johnson, Bryant and O’Neal. Reaves, Kessler, and the rotating wing defenders fit well beside him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pelicans’ Derik Queen finds Trey Murphy for epic alley-oop slam dunk
articles.summary: Jamahl Mosley’s New Orleans Pelicans battled the Oklahoma City Thunder on Friday, November 20 as guard Trey Murphy III was questionable with an injury issue...
articles.body:
Jamahl Mosley's New Orleans Pelicans battled the Oklahoma City Thunder on Friday, November 20 as guard Trey Murphy III was questionable with an injury issue. Forward Herb Jones was praised for recent improvements while Murphy III overcame his injury and took to the skies, throwing home a huge dunk on a pass from big man Derik Queen.

The excitement was palpable in the announcers' voices as Queen let the pass fly and Murphy III did the rest.

New Orleans shocked onlookers as it took a ten-point lead heading toward halftime with just over three minutes to go on the game clock. Zion Williamson paced Moseley's team with 18 points in 16 minutes while Saddiq Bey and Jeremiah Fears combined for 17 first half points at that stage of the game.

Veteran Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and rookie Aday Mara led the Thunder with 14 and 12 points, respectively, as they struggled to keep pace with Moseley's young, hungry Western Conference team.

The game came amid rumors of possible moves by the Minnesota Timberwolves and/or Pelicans to the NBA's Eastern Conference . The first half finished up with a score of 64-56 in favor of New Orleans as the Thunder shot just 6-of-18 from three-point land, although Mara helped pace them to a 30-24 edge in points in the paint.

The Pelicans' strong first half performance showed they have what it takes to complete with elite NBA franchises when they work together and Williamson plays up to his immense potential. Queen's arrival as a solid passing big man teamed well with Murphy III's scoring and Jones' defense on a night when fans expected a different first-half outcome.

articles.title: James Harden scores 51 points to propel Cleveland past Indiana 128-119
articles.summary: CLEVELAND (AP) — James Harden scored 51 points as the Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in an NBA Cup game on Friday night.It was the 1...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND (AP) — James Harden scored 51 points as the Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in an NBA Cup game on Friday night.

It was the 18-year veteran guard's 26th 50-point game, passing the late Kobe Bryant for third-most 50-point games in NBA history. It was Harden's first since he had 55 points for the Los Angeles Clippers against the Charlotte Hornets on Nov. 22, 2025.

Harden is the 15th player to have a 50-point game for Cleveland. It was also his best scoring game with the Cavaliers since being acquired near the trade deadline in February.

Harden was 15 of 26 from the field, including 7 of 11 from beyond the arc. He also made all 14 of his free throws along with six rebounds and six assists for the Cavaliers, who have won three of four and improved to 2-1 in East Group B.

Donovan Mitchell added 20 points. Peyton Watson, who missed Wednesday's game due to a lower back contusion after being injured on Monday against Chicago, scored 15.

Ivica Zubac had 21 points and 10 rebounds and Pascal Siakam scored 21 for the Pacers, who have dropped three straight and fell to 1-2 in East Group B.

Cleveland was up 74-73 four minutes into the third quarter before going on a 21-4 run over a nearly four-minute span. Harden scored 13 during the spurt as he made all four of his shots from the field, including a pair of 3-pointers.

The Cavaliers' largest lead was 113-90 with 7:39 remaining before the Pacers countered with a 21-4 run to make it a two-possession game with 2:03 left. Mitchell ended the spurt though with a basket on the ensuing trip.

"We experienced or witnessed conduct we considered to be verbal, emotional, and psychological abuse from Coach Fennelly," the former players said in a letter sent to the school. "We reported this and what we believed was inappropriate physical contact to members of the coaching staff and Iowa State athletic administration, but we do not believe our concerns were taken seriously. "Our individual experiences may differ, but we are united in our concerns about an environment where intimidation, humiliation, and fear became normalized," the letter continued. An Iowa State spokesperson confirmed that the school received the letter but offered no further comment, according to ESPN .

The incident in question occurred with two minutes remaining in the game. During a timeout, Fennelly yelled at sophomore guard Sienna Harvey and lightly pushed her head. Harvey didn't immediately react to the contact, and Fennelly continued his instructions in the Cyclones' huddle.

articles.title: James Harden Hyped as 'Top 10 All-Time' by Kenny Atkinson After Cavs Star's 51-Point Game
articles.summary: Cleveland Cavaliers head coach Kenny Atkinson called guard James Harden a "top 10" all-time NBA player after he scored 51 points in a 128-119 home win over the Indiana Pacers on Friday evening.
articles.body:
Cleveland Cavaliers head coach Kenny Atkinson called guard James Harden a "top 10" all-time NBA player after he scored 51 points in a 128-119 home win over the Indiana Pacers on Friday evening.

Atkinson made the remarks during his postgame press conference ( 6:15 mark ).

"Guy's special," Atkinson said. "We've got to appreciate this guy. This guy is top 10 of all time. I know I appreciate every day coaching him. It's an honor, I really mean that. Doesn't happen to a lot of coaches, to get to coach a guy like that."

Harden, an 18-year veteran, is an eight-time All-NBA player and three-time scoring champion. On Friday evening, he turned back the clock to his Houston Rockets days, when he dominated the league on a nightly basis, averaging 29.6 points per game for the team over eight-plus seasons (2012-13 to 2020-21).

Harden is now alone in third on the list of NBA players who have scored 50 or more points in a single regular season game ( 26 ). He was tied with Los Angeles Lakers legend Kobe Bryant heading into the evening. Wilt Chamberlain (118) and Michael Jordan (31) are first and second on the list.

articles.title: Dos días en el pasaje del terror
articles.standfirst: Horrible doble jornada de Euroliga de un Madrid irreconocible: anotando 20 puntos menos de su media, sin energía, con una mala defensa y jugadores muy por debajo de lo esperado
articles.summary: Horrible doble jornada de Euroliga de un Madrid irreconocible: anotando 20 puntos menos de su media, sin energía, con una mala defensa y jugadores muy por debajo de lo esperado
articles.body: Es tal el ritmo de la Euroliga que una semana basta para voltear cualquier realidad. Hace justo una semana este que escribe calificaba los partidos del Real Madrid de "parque de atracciones". El equipo volaba, encandilaba a su parroquia, reventaba defensas y raro era el día que no alcanzaba los 100 puntos. Dos jornadas después, los blancos se han bajado de la montaña rusa y se han metido en el pasaje del terror. Lo que todo era la fluidez, puntería y efervescencia se ha transformado en los últimos dos partidos en espesura, desatino y juego plano. Ni rastro del Madrid que había ganado 14 de los últimos 15 partidos y cuya única derrota había sido ante el poderoso Panathinaikos en la prórroga tras una actuación muy meritoria. Ante el Besiktas (83-79), fue una cita trampa, contra un rival sin nombre pero que es un conjunto serio y estaba extramotivado por recibir por primera vez en su casa al club más laureado de Europa. Frente al Olympiacos (92-76), fue atropellado por el vigente campeón, sí, pero mermado por las ausencias de Jean Montero, Milutinov y Dorsey. En apenas 48 horas, el Madrid firmó dos de sus peores partidos de la temporada. Antes de subirse al avión y emprender rumbo al Este, promediaba más de 98 puntos por encuentro. Se quedó en 79 en Estambul y 76 en Atenas, su registro más bajo del curso empeorando los 77 que metió en Dubái. De media, 20 puntos menos esta semana. De 119,8 de valoración en lo que iba de temporada a 81 en las dos últimas citas. En ambas faltaron energía y piernas, como si el cansancio se hubiera apoderado de los jugadores. En ese aspecto, fueron arrollados por sus dos rivales. El Madrid lució una mala defensa, no pudo imponer su ritmo pese a ganar el rebote en ambos encuentros, no compartió el balón como acostumbraba (15,5 asistencias), los triples no fueron el gran argumento ofensivo que eran (19/61) y las pérdidas acabaron siendo un lastre más por el momento que por la cantidad (16 de media). Las siete que sumaron en los primeros minutos ante el Olympiacos fueron, según Pedro Martínez, "un gran problema porque tenemos falta de confianza a raíz de ellas". El entrenador madridista reconocía después del castañazo en Atenas que quizá ahora no estaban en un buen momento. "Hace dos días, tuvimos la misma sensación de falta de energía en comparación con el otro equipo. Seguro que jugar fuera de casa es más difícil, pero no basta para explicar lo que pasó. Estamos intentando hacerlo mejor. Los jugadores están intentando hacer las cosas bien, pero no estamos encontrando el buen baloncesto que hicimos en otros momentos de esta temporada". En cuanto a nombres propios, ahora sí se ha echado de menos a Facundo Campazzo y el trabajo oscuro pero eficiente de Mikael Jantunen. Bajo momento de Jaime Pradilla y Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot. Sería absurdo dudar de una calidad contrastadísima, pero ambos andan lejos de su condición de fichajes estelares para este proyecto. Andrés Feliz ha estado en este viaje por debajo de lo mostrado antes. Nick Smith Jr. dejó brotes verdes ante el Besiktas y fueron pisoteados ante el Olympiacos. De lo poco positivo de estos días, la aportación de Damian Jones pese a sus lagunas defensivas y el regreso de Theo Maledon, el mejor en los tres partidos tras superar su lesión, aunque en los dos últimos sus estadísticas tuvieran escasa incidencia. Eli John Ndiaye se reestrenó en Atenas como madridista. Poco pudo hacer. Ayudará, pero justo ante el Olympiacos no era el día más sencillo para volver. Con la clasificación tan apretada, un par de triunfos te llevan al ático y dos derrotas te hacen caer por las escaleras. El lunes, el Madrid era quinto, a un paso de los puestos que dan el factor cancha en playoffs. El viernes, es noveno, en zona de play-in. Así es esta Euroliga, tan apasionante como cruel. No perdona los malos días. Y no digamos las malas rachas. Este domingo ante el Asisa Joventut y el miércoles ante el Zalgiris, ambos en el Movistar Arena, serán momentos para comprobar si la peor semana del año deja efectos secundarios.

articles.title: NBA Cup 2026: James Harden puts up 51 in Cavs' win over Pacers; shorthanded Raptors fend off Pistons, end 6-game skid
articles.summary: Harden recorded his first 50-piece with Cleveland, and Toronto's Scottie Barnes one-upped Detroit's Cade Cunningham in the clutch.
articles.body:
James Harden played by far his best game in a Cleveland Cavaliers uniform on Friday night during NBA Cup group play.

The 37-year-old guard erupted for 51 points in a 128-119 home win over the Indiana Pacers, a season high and his most since joining the Cavaliers amid the 2025-26 campaign.

Cleveland (9-8) improved to 2-1 in Cup competition, knocking on the Miami Heat's door atop East Group B. Indiana (5-11), which trailed the Cavaliers by as many as 24 points, dropped to 1-2 in this year's NBA Cup.

Harden shot 15 of 26 from the floor, including 7 of 11 from beyond the arc. He also finished 14 of 14 from the charity stripe and with six rebounds and six assists. The one-time NBA MVP and 11-time All-Star now has the third-most 50-plus-point games in NBA history . With 26 such performances, he passed the late Kobe Bryant (25) on Friday and now trails Michael Jordan (31) and Wilt Chamberlain (118) in that category.

While collecting his first 50-piece with the Cavaliers, Harden moved into ninth all-time for most combined NBA regular and postseason points . His handles were on full display . He rained down 3s, and he made an impact at the rim .

Raptors' Scottie Barnes, Pistons' Cade Cunningham trade blows in thriller

Toronto came into Friday missing a trio of starters and on a six-game losing streak. Darko Rajaković's team was playing without RJ Barrett, Collin Murray-Boyles and, of course, Kawhi Leonard, who's still working his way back from a knee injury.

And yet, the shorthanded Raptors (6-10) found a way on the road versus the Detroit Pistons (10-5) in NBA Cup action, ending their skid with a riveting 105-102 win .

It's important to note that Detroit isn't at full strength, either. Jalen Duren remains sidelined with a hamstring issue . Plus, Duncan Robinson is out with a quad strain .

The absence of some star power didn't diminish what turned out to be an incredible matchup between two squads in East Group A and between a pair of former Montverde Academy teammates. Toronto's Scottie Barnes and Detroit's Cade Cunningham went toe-to-toe, particularly down the stretch.

Cunningham, who clocked out with 23 points and nine assists, hit a go-ahead 3-pointer over Barnes with less than 20 seconds remaining. Then, with the Raptors down one point, Barnes drove on Cunningham and reclaimed the lead.

Cunningham tried to answer back but ended up with nowhere to go with the ball after picking up his dribble en route to the basket. He passed it, and Toronto rookie Allen Graves nabbed a steal that helped wrap up the victory.

Barnes had 29 points, 5 rebounds and 5 assists. Graves, a first-round pick from Santa Clara making his first career start, piled up 20 points, 10 rebounds and 3 steals.

After that nail-biter, Toronto is 2-1 in East Group A, whereas Detroit is 1-1. The bottom dweller of the group, the Milwaukee Bucks (0-2 in NBA Cup play), was eliminated from knockout-round contention because the Raptors and Orlando Magic both won on Friday.

The Magic left Brooklyn victorious 113-111 , thanks to Franz Wagner, who scored 35 points on 13-of-25 shooting and knocked down a game-winning jumper with 2.4 ticks left against the Nets.

Orlando is 3-0 in NBA Cup games this year.

Note: * denotes teams that have been eliminated from knockout round contention.

articles.title: Bestial Aday Mara
articles.standfirst: El pívot español de los Thunder bate sus topes en puntos y rebotes con 22+16, una actuación nunca vista en un novato en la historia de a franquicia
articles.summary: El pívot español de los Thunder bate sus topes en puntos y rebotes con 22+16, una actuación nunca vista en un novato en la historia de a franquicia
articles.body: En la mejor noche de su corta carrera en la NBA, Aday Mara destrozó a los Pelicans con 22 puntos y 16 rebotes. No sólo fue su cuarto doble-doble en 16 encuentros en la NBA ni sus topes personales en ambas estadísticas es que ningún novato en la historia de los Thunder había vivido una actuación así. El pívot español, de nuevo titular, hizo 11/15 en tiros de campo. Machacó todo lo que le llegó ya fuera tras un alley-oop, encontrando un pasillo hacia el aro o después de uno de sus siete rebotes ofensivos, su segundo mejor registro en la NBA. Algún 2+1 le podían haber señalizado. Pero también dejó muestras de su gran juego de pies. A más de un defensor le volvió loco con sus movimientos hacia el centro de la zona o por línea de fondo. Aderezó su bestial actuación con dos asistencias y dos tapones. Con él en pista, +15 para su equipo, el mejor dato entre quienes salieron de inicio. Y, lo que es importante: él luce, crece y, lejos de firmar actuaciones vacías, ayuda a ganar a unos Thunder necesitados de victorias. Vencieron en la NBA Cup (2-1): 126-120. "Sé que lo puedo hacer mucho mejor", aseguró Mara, que dijo estar centrado en "ayudar al equipo". Vaya si lo está haciendo en plena tortura de lesiones. Los Thunder no tuvieron a Alex Caruso, Cason Wallace, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Nikola Topic, ni a Thomas Sorber. Las ausencias las está aprovechando el español, que ante Nueva Orleans se fue a los 29 minutos, su segunda mejor marca en la NBA. La exhibición de Mara, por supuesto, acaparó elogios en la sala de prensa. "Es muy grande, juega alegre, tiene talento y protege muy bien el aro. La gente ve eso, pero creo que resulta más invisible su inteligencia. Realmente tiene un gran sentido para el juego", aseguró el entrenador Mark Daigneault. Pero Mara también tiene una doble cara en el lado más positivo. Es muy agradable, bromista y bonachón fuera de la pista. Dentro, se transforma. "Y en segundo lugar -continuó Daignealut- es un tremendo competidor. Igual su personalidad, porque es muy amigable, engaña, pero ese tío sale a la pista a competir". Muy mejorado físicamente desde que aterrizó en la NBA como número 12 del pasado draft, a Mara cuesta arrebatarle un rebote, juega duro, celebra con rabia... Aunque aún le falte experiencia, tiene el toque necesario de mala leche para sobrevivir en el campo de batalla que son las zonas de la NBA. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander anotó 40 puntos y una jugada de tres puntos que dejó el partido sentenciado a falta de 34 segundos (124-116). Tuvieron que remontar los Thunder, que se vieron 16 abajo en el tercer cuarto. Jared McCain y el novato Bennett Stirtz ayudaron con 18 puntos por cabeza a un equipo que va sobreviviendo pese a las lesiones de tres titulares: 8-5 desde entonces. Entre las alegrías, ver el crecimiento de Mara, referencia ya en lo que debería ser su periodo de adaptación. "Esto es sólo el comienzo para mí y estoy emocionado por lo que viene", advierte.

The Cavaliers' largest lead was 113-90 with 7:39 remaining before the Pacers countered with a 21-4 run to make it a two-possession game with 2:03 left. Mitchell ended the spurt though with a basket on the ensuing trip.

"When you talk about just basketball, obviously Wilt was elite, but you got Mike and Kobe, shooting guard position, the best to ever do it. So just to be in that conversation, it's very humbling and it's definitely special," Harden said.

Harden's game has evolved over the past couple seasons where he is counted on more for getting open shots for teammates than being the prolific scorer he was during his first 12 years in the league.

On Friday night though, he showed that he can still have games that leave fans and team-mates in awe.

"It's a different role for me. My usage rate isn't extremely high every game. We have somebody for that. So mine is kind of scoring when I need to, but then distributing the ball," Harden continued.

"My number is called and you need to go out there and put the shots up. Ok, I can still do it. I knew I can do it, but it's just when you don't do something consistently and then it goes away a little bit or you just don't know if you got it or not."

articles.title: James Harden passes Kobe Bryant for 50-point NBA games
articles.summary: James Harden moves third on the all-time list for 50-point NBA games as the Cleveland Cavaliers beat the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in the NBA Cup.
articles.body:
James Harden scored 51 points to move third on the all-time list for 50-point NBA games as the Cleveland Cavaliers beat the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in the NBA Cup.

The 37-year-old made all 14 of his free throws as his recorded his 26th 50-point game to move above the legendary Kobe Bryant.

Harden, who also made six rebounds and provided six assists at Rocket Arena in Cleveland, had not passed 50 points since scoring 55 for the Los Angeles Clippers in November 2025.

Legendary centre Wilt Chamberlain holds the NBA record ⁠with 118 50-point games, while Michael Jordan is second with 31.

"When you talk about just basketball, obviously Wilt was elite, but you got Mike and Kobe - shooting guard position, the best to ever do it - so just to be in that conversation, it's very humbling and it's definitely special," said an emotional Harden.

Aged 37 years and 86 days, he is the fourth oldest player to score 50 points in a game.

"What excites me a lot is even being in my 18th year learning how to still be impactful," said Harden, the ninth highest scorer in NBA history with 29,633 points.

"It's easy when you're young - 23, 24, you run around, you jump high and can move fast and get by. Now it's like, you're not as fast.

"That's the evolution of James Harden and figuring that out.

"Tonight was a confidence-booster that I can do it at a high level still."

The Cavaliers travel to the Chicago Bulls in the NBA on Tuesday.

articles.body: El alero del Barça Joel Parra, expulsado con doble técnica en el último minuto del partido que los azulgranas perdieron este viernes en el Palau Blaugrana contra el Estrella Roja de Belgrado (100-103), ha asegurado que el arbitraje ha sido "una falta de respeto". "Los árbitros nos han faltado al respeto. Más allá de que nos puedan pitar una falta o no, hoy ha sido una falta de respeto al club y a nuestra gente que ha venido al Palau a animarnos", ha afirmado el internacional español en declaraciones a los medios de comunicación en el vestuario local. Parra, antes de abandonar la pista visiblemente enfadado, mostró el escudo de la camiseta con vehemencia a los tres colegiados, un gesto que ha explicado después: "Lo he hecho para recordarles que somos el Barça, un club histórico y propietario de la Euroliga. Merecemos más respeto. Cuando vamos a otras pistas no tenemos la misma sensación que cuando los equipos vienen aquí". Con todo, el alero ha señalado atribuir la derrota al arbitraje sería "un error", puesto que "en muchos tramos del partido" el Barça ha "dejado de jugar en ataque y en defensa". También el entrenador Aleksander Sekulic tuvo palabras para la actuación de los árbitros. "Ha sido un partido duro, decidido en el último momento. Hemos jugado al límite y quiero aclarar que hemos perdido por nuestros errores, sobre todo por nuestras pérdidas, pero hay cosas que no puedo entender, más aún cuando jugamos en casa, como la diferencia en las faltas y los tiros libres (16 a 30). articles.body:
James Harden scored a season-high 51 points – moving into third place in NBA history ‌with his 26th career 50-point game – while leading the Cleveland Cavaliers to a 128-119 win over the visiting Indiana Pacers.

Harden, 37, made 15 of 26 field-goal ⁠attempts, 7 of 11 3-point shots and ⁠all 14 of his free throws while breaking a tie with Kobe Bryant on the 50-point list. Wilt Chamberlain holds the NBA record with 118 50-point games, and Michael Jordan is second with 31.

Donovan Mitchell added 20 points for Cleveland on a night when all NBA games were part of the NBA Cup’s ⁠group stage. The Cavaliers earned their third win in the past four games overall.

Pascal Siakam and Ivica Zubac each scored 21 for Indiana, which took its third consecutive loss.

Jalen Johnson compiled 26 points, six rebounds and six assists to help Atlanta post a victory over visiting Charlotte.

Aaron Wiggins scored 19 points, and Nickeil Alexander-Walker added 17 for the Hawks, who won their third ⁠straight game and their seventh in nine tries. Atlanta trailed by 14 points in the first half.

Moussa Diabate produced 21 points and 15 rebounds while Brandon Miller scored 19 points for the Hornets, who lost their fourth straight game.

Franz Wagner capped a stellar 35-point performance with a tiebreaking stepback jumper over two defenders with 2.8 seconds left as Orlando outlasted Brooklyn in New York.

Wagner made 13 of 25 shots as the Magic beat the Nets for the 10th straight time. Orlando’s Desmond Bane hit seven 3-pointers for his 21 points.

Julius Randle collected 27 points, nine rebounds and six ‌assists for the Nets, but he missed a last-second 3-point attempt. Day’Ron Sharpe contributed 17 points and 11 boards as Brooklyn took its fourth loss in a row.

Toronto Raptors 105, Detroit Pistons 102

Scottie Barnes had 29 points, including a go-ahead basket in the final minute, and visiting Toronto snapped a six-game losing streak by edging Detroit.

Raptors rookie Allen Graves, making his first start, supplied career highs of 20 points and 10 rebounds while Immanuel Quickley notched 18 points and 10 assists.

Cade Cunningham totalled 23 points and nine assists as the Pistons took just their second loss in six games. Kevin Huerter added 20 points.

Oklahoma City Thunder 126, New Orleans Pelicans 120

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 40 points to lead Oklahoma City past visiting New Orleans, just the Thunder’s second win in the past six games.

Rookie Aday Mara had career highs of 22 points and 16 rebounds for Oklahoma City. The Thunder shot 53.3% from the field, their second-best effort of the season.

Zion ⁠Williamson and Jeremiah Fears each scored 22 points for the Pelicans, who took their eighth loss in nine games.

Nikola Jokic had ⁠24 of his 26 points after halftime and added 11 assists as host Denver overcame a triple-double by Alperen Sengun to beat Houston.

Christian Braun and Cameron Johnson scored 19 points each for the Nuggets, who won their second straight contest. The game featured 32 lead changes, the most in the NBA this season.

Sengun finished with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for the Rockets, who had won five of their previous six games. Fred VanVleet ⁠put up 25 points.

Los Angeles Lakers 106, Sacramento Kings 104

Luka Doncic scored 25 points and dished out eight assists as Los Angeles rallied past visiting Sacramento, avoiding what would have been the Lakers’ first set of consecutive losses this season.

Walker Kessler added 15 points as the Lakers came out on top ⁠after their nine-game winning streak ended Wednesday in a loss to the Utah Jazz.

De’Andre Hunter scored 30 points, and ⁠Domantas Sabonis added 19 points and 16 rebounds as the Kings dropped their eighth straight game. Sacramento led by as many as 11 points in the third quarter.

Anthony Davis finished with game highs of 36 points and 11 rebounds as Washington rallied from a 15-point deficit to down host Chicago.

Davis also made a key play on defence when he disrupted Norman Powell’s potential game-tying layup attempt with six seconds remaining to force a miss. Wizards rookie AJ Dybantsa ‌posted 20 points, 10 rebounds and six assists.

Collin Gillespie added 16 points ‌and ‌three 3-pointers off the bench, and Jalen Green scored 14 for the Suns, who have won five of seven. At 8-7, Phoenix is over .500 for the first time this season.

Rookie Darryn Peterson had 20 points and set his season highs in rebounds (10) and assists (eight) while recording his first career double-double. Jaxson Hayes added 18 points and a season-best 14 boards for the Jazz, who had won their previous two after a 1-13 start.

articles.title: NBA Trade Idea To Swap Zion Williamson for 3 Players, 4 Draft Picks
articles.summary: The Charlotte Hornets are unsurprisingly short on offensive punch after trading away LaMelo Ball during the offseason, while the New Orleans Pelicans should be strongly considering a teardown.
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets are unsurprisingly short on offensive punch after trading away LaMelo Ball during the offseason, while the New Orleans Pelicans should be strongly considering a teardown.

Though injuries to Kon Knueppel, Brandon Miller and Coby White have plenty to do with it, this year's Hornets are nothing like the supercharged bunch that scored more efficiently than any team in the league after Christmas last season. They need someone to attack all the space in the middle of the floor if and when their long-range bombers remember how to shoot.

Meanwhile, the Pelicans are circling the drain. Amid blowout losses, offensive struggles and trade demands from underperforming players, it feels like New Orleans is at a crossroads with its current core.

Let's cook up a Zion Williamson trade to clean up both of those messes.

Charlotte Hornets Acquire: Zion Williamson

New Orleans Pelicans Acquire: Dennis Schroder, Grant Williams, Tidjane Salaun, 2027 first-round pick (via DAL; protected 1-2), 2027 first-round pick (via MIA; 15-30), 2027 second-round pick (via MEM), 2027 second-round pick (NOP's own)

This would be an easier sell if the Charlotte Hornets' best offensive players had been healthy all year, but you can still understand the theoretical appeal of Zion Williamson barreling downhill in an offense with maximum spacing from Kon Knueppel, Brandon Miller, Coby White and Naz Reid.

Williamson is attacking the rim more often than at any point since 2022-23, when he last earned an All-Star nod. He's taking 73.0 percent of his attempts at point-blank range and driving the ball 13.9 times per game. Williamson's 52.8 percent finishing rate on drives is solid, sitting right in the range of players like Deni Avdija and Dylan Harper.

He's doing all that in the spacing wasteland of New Orleans, where neither centers nor point guards scare defenders enough to open up the lane. Just imagine the havoc he'd wreak in Hornets head coach Charles Lee's system. Plus, any team that sent out LaMelo Ball in an offseason trade could use some additional playmaking at other positions. He hasn't played the role much lately, but we're not so far removed from the days of "Point Zion" routinely averaging around 5.0 assists per game.

Beyond making tactical sense, Williamson's contract also fits Charlotte's finances pretty cleanly. The Hornets can match salaries easily enough without giving up integral pieces. Only Schroder's deal extends beyond this year. Rookie Christian Anderson is ticketed to play backup point guard going forward.

New Orleans is due for a hard reset. Moving Williamson is a logical step in that process—especially right now, when the notoriously injury-prone forward is healthy and playing well.

Even if the Pelicans could count on Williamson to sustain his current form through the balance of his deal (he's due a non-guaranteed $44.9 million for 2027-28), his fit with Derik Queen is abysmal. It's only slightly less difficult to justify keeping him in a prominent role, with Jeremiah Fears being such an on-ball development priority.

Because New Orleans could simply wipe Williamson's money off the books this summer, it won't want a ton of salary coming back in a trade. Schroder is the only incoming player with 2027-28 money left on his deal. He might also make sense as a backup, assuming Dejounte Murray is on the way out.

The Pels get a pair of immediate first-rounders here, one of which has a great chance of landing in the lottery. In addition to that, the additional seconds could be used in a package to trade up into the back of the 2027 first round. In that hypothetical, New Orleans could add as many as three first-round talents in the upcoming draft. For a team that needs a cost-controlled, young-talent infusion, that's enticing.

articles.title: “Plagiarism”: 6-Foot-11 Rockets Star Responds to Victor Wembanyama’s Viral Move With Evidence
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama has once again gone viral for showcasing his extraordinary ability around the rim. The San Antonio Spurs superstar caught attention with an...
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama has once again gone viral for showcasing his extraordinary ability around the rim. The San Antonio Spurs superstar caught attention with an unusual dunk-like finish. However, the viral moment also brought back an old clip of center Steven Adams performing a remarkably similar move, prompting a hilarious reaction from the veteran big man.

The Houston Rockets star accused Wemby of plagiarism. The banter began when an account shared an old video of the New Zealand center scoring a shunk during a pre-game warm-up routine.

The clip showed the 6-foot-11 veteran executing the move, prompting the account to draw a comparison with Victor Wembanyama's recently viral moment. Sharing the footage, the account captioned the post: "@stevenadams 4 years before Wemby." Adams clearly enjoyed the comparison and decided to join the conversation.

Taking to his Instagram story, the veteran center tagged Victor Wembanyama and wrote , "@wemby Plagiarism."And in another line, the response quickly added a humorous twist to the comparison. By invoking Ravenclaw, one of the four houses from the Harry Potter universe, Adams wrote: "Deduct 10 points from Ravenclaw @spurs."

Victor Wembanyama has already become one of the league's most fascinating players, regularly producing viral moments. However, this time, Adams was quick to remind everyone that he might have been performing the move long before it became associated with the Spurs sensation.

The unusual moment came during the fourth quarter of the Spurs' matchup against the Los Angeles Clippers. With 3:34 remaining on the clock, Victor Wembanyama found himself running into open space after teammate Stephon Castle grabbed a rebound and delivered a pass ahead. The Frenchman caught the ball near the basket. Given his 7-foot-4 frame and incredible reach, a powerful slam dunk seemed inevitable. However, Wemby had something different in mind.

Instead of throwing the ball down through the rim, he jumped towards the basket and released the ball with a soft, jump-shot-like flick while hovering just above the rim. The ball dropped through the net, leaving viewers surprised by the unconventional finish.

The move immediately caught the attention of the broadcast team. Spurs color commentator and former NBA player Sean Elliott came up with a name for the unusual finish, calling it a "shunk." The NBA also shared the footage on its official social media account, asking fans, "Did Wemby just… shoot it from above the rim???"

Apart from fans and Adams, Victor Wembanyama's unusual finish also caught the attention of his Spurs teammates. Center Luke Kornet was particularly impressed by the creativity behind the move. "It's very fun. I'm a big fan of it."

Kornet even joked about trying something similar himself, adding to the light-hearted reaction surrounding Victor Wembanyama's latest viral highlight. But after the game, Wemby revealed that the unusual finish was not simply another highlight.

Previously against the Detroit Pistons, Victor Wembanyama threw the ball off the backboard before catching it in mid-air and finishing with a powerful one-handed dunk. Against the Clippers, it was a different story.

The 7-foot-4 center had been dealing with a painful blister on the middle finger of his right hand, which had been aggravated by his frequent dunking.

"I'm not gonna lie, I've had this blister forever, and it's killing me. Every time I dunk, it kills me." Wembanyama said after the game to the reporters . He further explained that the blister had likely developed because of how frequently he had been dunking throughout the season.

"So I did not [quit dunking], but if I can avoid it, I would," Wemby added.

Interestingly, Victor Wembanyama entered the contest as the NBA's leading dunker, with 72 dunks through 16 games. The unconventional finish was even officially recorded as a dunk. Despite the injury concern, he finished the night with an impressive 32 points, 11 rebounds, three assists, one steal, and one block in 33 minutes as San Antonio secured a 124-112 victory over the Clippers.

articles.title: Indiana Fever plan to fire head coach Stephanie White, says Rachel DeMita
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever have reportedly made up their mind about the future of Stephanie White. Following an underwhelming run in the 2026 WNBA Playoffs, the India...
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever have reportedly made up their mind about the future of Stephanie White.

Following an underwhelming run in the 2026 WNBA Playoffs, the Indiana Fever changed their approach ahead of the new season.

The franchise did so by firing GM Amber Cox, and the same day, president Kelly Krauskopf stepped down as well.

Despite these changes, the Fever fanbase still weren't happy, as they wanted to see head coach Stephanie White also follow in their footsteps to start with a clean slate.

Rachel DeMita is certain Stephanie White 'isn't staying' with Indiana Fever

Under coach White, the Fever are yet to miss the postseason, but the real issue that fans have with her is the lack of Caitlin Clark's proper usage.

Keeping that in mind, WNBA analyst Rachel DeMita isn't convinced that the Fever ownership would go ahead with White after cleansing the front office.

"We're also reading between the lines on other things that we've heard. And it's like, 'No, Coach Stephanie White isn't staying.'"

"When they bring in this new executive in charge of basketball operations… maybe it's their decision on if they want to keep this coaching staff or if they want to go with somebody else," DeMita said.

She added, "There are so many variables. You get in a new coaching staff. You can play a different style of offense; you can play a different style of defense.

"If you get in a new front office, but keep the coaching staff and then rearrange the roster, maybe everything looks different."

All things considered, no concrete decision has been made by the Fever ownership, but if you were to believe they are inclining towards parting ways with White.

If that happens, it would be the second time a Fever head coach has lost their job since the franchise drafted Clark.

But if moving on from White is what it takes to keep Clark happy, the Fever ownership would likely side with their cornerstone superstar.

articles.title: 3 most overrated NBA teams in 2026 season
articles.summary: These 3 NBA teams are not as good as people think.
articles.body:
A month and a half into the NBA season, early evaluations are taking shape as fans get a better sense of where their team stands. The Lakers, 76ers, and Spurs have justified the pre-season optimism, while teams like the Knicks, Nuggets, and Cavaliers have fallen short.

Several unexpected teams have surged up the standings, raising serious questions about whether their early momentum is sustainable. With that in mind, these are the three most overrated teams in the NBA right now.

Miami acquired Giannis this offseason in hopes of thrusting their team into contention. Early on, that plan seemed to backfire, opening the season 0-4, but had a resurgence, going 9-2 in their last 11. So, why are they atop this list?

Though Miami has gotten better as the season has progressed, there are still major concerns surrounding the roster. Breaking down their losses tells the story: They came up short to two mid-tier teams in close games – the Hornets and the Mavericks – alongside blowout losses to the Warriors, Lakers, Timberwolves, and Pistons by a total margin of 83 points.

They have some good wins, but the inconsistencies and lack of good play against true contenders are extremely concerning moving forward.

Between Ty Jerome's breakout and Rookie Cameron Boozer's stellar start, the Grizzlies are sitting pretty with an 11-4 record tied for 4th in the Western Conference. Yet, their record doesn't reflect the legitimacy of their ranking.

Memphis has taken full advantage of their strength of schedule. They have two notable wins: a 21-point blowout win in Portland against the Trailblazers and a three-point victory over the Cavaliers decided by game-sealing free throws. Outside of those 2 wins, their opponents hold a combined record of just 30-76(.283%).

It's tough to get an accurate read on Memphis given their weak slate of opponents, so for now, I'm not sold on their early success.

The Hawks are 9-6 and sit fifth in the Eastern Conference, level with Miami and behind them only on a tiebreaker. That's a solid start on the surface, but a closer look at Atlanta's résumé tells a different story.

The Hawks have just one win over a team with a winning record, a five-point road win over the Thunder. Add a three-point win over the .500 Cavaliers, and that's the entire list of quality wins. The teams they've beaten otherwise hold a combined record of just 29-75 (.279). Even against that soft group, Atlanta hasn't been dominant: five of those seven wins came by seven points or fewer, including narrow escapes against the Nets and Pacers.

Until the Hawks start beating good teams, their record looks more like the result of an easy schedule than a sign they belong near the top of the East.

articles.title: James Harden becomes 4th-oldest player to score 50: 'I can still do it'
articles.summary: Harden has cemented himself as one of the NBA's best scorers ever
articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers' February trade for James Harden hasn't aged great, but he reminded general manager Koby Altman why he made the deal last night against the Indiana Pacers . Harden, 37, turned back the clock for a 51-point performance, becoming the fourth-oldest player in NBA history to score 50+.

It's a star-studded list Harden is joining, as Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant and three-time Sixth Man of the Year Jamal Crawford are the other three players. Bryant has the highest-scoring game of the four, tallying 60 points in his memorable final performance against the Utah Jazz .

Harden, who passed Bryant for the third-most 50-point games in NBA history, converted 15 of his 26 shots and 7 of his 11 3-pointers. It helped bring a crucial win to Cleveland, which stumbled to an 8-8 start this season after an Eastern Conference Finals run.

The performance also reminded Harden just how elite of a scorer he can be despite becoming more of a playmaker in recent years.

"It's a different role for me," Harden said . "My usage rate isn't extremely high every game. We have somebody for that. So mine is kind of scoring when I need to, but then distributing the ball. My number is called and you need to go out there and put the shots up. OK, I can still do it. I knew I can do it, but it's just when you don't do something consistently and then it goes away a little bit or you just don't know if you got it or not."

Now, whether Harden can string together games like this in the playoffs is a different question.

articles.title: Luka Makes NBA History, Full Box Score Stats & Highlights for Acuff, Top Lakers & Kings Players
articles.summary: On a night when Luka Dončić failed to score 30 points for the second consecutive game, the Los Angeles Lakers still rallied late to earn a 106-104 win over the Sacramento Kings on Friday night.
articles.body:
On a night when Luka Dončić failed to score 30 points for the second consecutive game, the Los Angeles Lakers still rallied late to earn a 106-104 win over the Sacramento Kings on Friday night.

Dončić put up 25 points in 36 minutes, though he did make NBA history in the process as the fastest player to reach 550 points, 100 rebounds and 100 assists in a season.

Quentin Grimes played the role of hero again for the Lakers with the go-ahead three in the final minute. Zach LaVine finished with 19 points and a season-high seven rebounds in the loss.

Dončić's 25 points marked his second-lowest scoring output of the season, but made up for it by dishing out a team-high eight assists in the win. He also made history by tying his own record as the fastest player to reach 550 points, 100 rebounds and 100 assists in a season, doing so in his 15th game.

The absence of Austin Reaves has allowed defenses to hone in more on Dončić, who is being double-teamed at an astronomical rate right now.

With more attention coming Dončić's way than normal, Grimes has really stepped up to provide the Lakers a viable No. 2 scoring option. He put up 47 earlier in the week against the Utah Jazz.

The Kings held Grimes to just 13 points on 2-of-7 shooting, but he came through in the clutch with a three that put the Lakers up 106-103 with 57 seconds left to play.

In a losing effort for the Kings, Darius Acuff Jr. put up 18 points and 12 assists in 36 minutes. It was his fourth double-double of the season, one behind Cameron Boozer for the rookie lead.

The difference in the game came from bench production. Kings reserves scored just five points on 1-of-11 shooting. The Lakers got 34 points from their bench, led by Collin Sexton's 10 points in 18 minutes.

The win gets the Lakers back on track after Wednesday's defeat against the Jazz snapped their nine-game winning streak. They are back atop the Western Conference standings with a 14-3 record and remain in second place in West Group C in the NBA Cup.

Dončić and the Lakers get two days off before returning to action on Monday when they host the Jazz again. Sacramento will look to end its seven-game losing streak in the second night of a back-to-back on Saturday against the Boston Celtics.

articles.title: NBA Cup 2026 Standings, Bracket Predictions After November 20 Group Play
articles.summary: Friday's NBA Cup results set up some fascinating situations across the majority of the six groups.
articles.body:
Friday's NBA Cup results set up some fascinating situations across the majority of the six groups.

The Denver Nuggets, Oklahoma City Thunder and Los Angeles Lakers all used wins on Friday night to set up massive clashes next week with the first-place teams in their respective groups.

The Orlando Magic are the closest team to capturing a group title. They moved to 3-0 in East Group A with a victory against the Brooklyn Nets. Orlando needs one more win to secure a spot in the eight-team knockout round.

The six group winners, as well as the best second-place team in each conference, advance to the quarterfinals.

1. Orlando (3-0; +17 point differential)

The Orlando Magic are the closest team to the knockout round in the Eastern Conference after Friday's games.

All Orlando needs to do is beat the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday at home and it will win East Group A.

Franz Wagner and Co. eked out a road win over the Brooklyn Nets on Friday to keep their edge over Detroit and the Toronto Raptors.

Toronto needs to run up the score on the Nets next Friday to have a shot at advancing as the best second-place team in the East. The Raptors are currently third in the best second-place team standings because of their low point differential.

East Group B is still wide open. The Cleveland Cavaliers' win over the Indiana Pacers on Friday was the expected result in the most loaded group of the three in the East.

The Miami Heat visit the Philadelphia 76ers on Wednesday. That's the game that will decide the direction of East Group B.

Philadelphia owns the best record in the Eastern Conference. A home win over Miami is expected for LeBron James, Joel Embiid and Co.

A win over Miami would likely secure the group title for the Sixers because it's assumed they would go on the road and defeat the Indiana Pacers, which they have already done once this season, and clinch the Group B title on Friday.

The Heat are in danger of missing the knockout round if they lose to the Sixers and then to the New York Knicks on Friday.

The Knicks host the Cavaliers on Wednesday and then the Heat two days later. They still have an outside chance to finish second in East Group B if they win both of those games.

The Boston Celtics are still in control of East Group C. They need to beat the Washington Wizards on the road on Tuesday and then the Atlanta Hawks at home on Friday to go 4-0 and top the group.

A second loss for both the Wizards and the Hawks might take them out of the best second-place team conversation.

Toronto needs a lot to happen in its favor, but if Boston and New York both win twice, it opens the door for the Raptors to be one of the only one-loss second-place teams left in the East.

Friday's results in the Western Conference set the stage for three blockbuster showdowns to determine each of the three groups next week.

The Denver Nuggets moved to 2-0 in West Group A thanks to a win over the Houston Rockets.

Nikola Jokic and Co. host Cooper Flagg and the Dallas Mavericks on Tuesday night to likely determine the Group A winner.

The Nuggets finish up group play against the Utah Jazz on Friday, so if they beat the Mavs, they have a strong chance of finishing first. The Mavs have a tougher conclusion with a trip to face the Phoenix Suns on Friday.

The Oklahoma City Thunder face a must-win on Wednesday night at home against the Minnesota Timberwolves.

OKC can't win the group with that result alone, but it will be in a good position to claim first with a win over the Wolves.

The LA Clippers own the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Thunder. They visit the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday in what will feel like an elimination game.

OKC will be rooting for Memphis so that a win over the Wolves takes it to the top of Group B thanks to head-to-head wins over the Wolves and Grizzlies.

The Wolves and Grizzlies play Friday. That could be for first place in Group B if the Wolves beat OKC and the Grizzlies beat the Clippers.

Group C has a Friday night showdown set up between the Los Angeles Lakers and San Antonio Spurs for first place.

The Spurs have to win in Portland on Wednesday to set up the clash for first place. They've already won in Oregon by 22 points earlier this month.

Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs will have the advantage because of home court against the Lakers.

A handful of teams will be rooting for the Spurs in that matchup because it would knock the Lakers to two losses in group play, which would likely eliminate them from advancing.

articles.title: Watch Bulls Mascot Play GTA 6 and Ignore Wizards Players' Intros in Viral Video
