Grand Theft Auto fever has been everywhere this week, including at the United Center on Friday night when Benny The Bull was busy playing the new game in the franchise during pregame intros.

The Chicago Bulls posted a video of their mascot playing GTA 6 during the pregame player intros for the Washington Wizards.

Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday, marking the first new release title in the popular franchise in 13 years. The wait proved to be worth it with the game generating $3.79 billion in first-day sales.

Benny probably wishes he would have spent the entire game playing Grand Theft Auto 6 because the Bulls weren't providing much entertainment in a 98-94 loss to the Wizards, who snapped their eight-game losing streak.

articles.title: JuJu Watkins Loses Her Voice from Illness, USC Star Drops Impressive Box-Score Stats & Reacts to Win
articles.summary: Not even a cold could prevent JuJu Watkins from turning in a dominant performance in USC's 78-69 victory over Baylor on Friday night at the Intuit Dome.
articles.body:
Not even a cold could prevent JuJu Watkins from turning in a dominant performance in USC's 78-69 victory over Baylor on Friday night at the Intuit Dome.

Watkins had a double-double with 36 points, 11 rebounds and a career-high six steals, while playing 39 out of 40 minutes.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Watkins revealed her illness at one point took away most of her voice.

"I'm feeling a little better," Watkins said. "It's one of the best feelings to be out here."

Friday's game marked Watkins' 19th double-double in 72 career college games. She has two 30-point double-doubles in five games to start this season. The senior standout also moved into third place in USC history for most career games with at least 35 points.

Making Watkins' early-season play even more impressive is she's dominating after missing all of the 2025-26 campaign due to a torn ACL.

"I've been for so long so honestly I'm taking every game and trying to learn as much as possible and translate it to the next game," Watkins said after the win about getting her legs back under her.

You would never know through five games that Watkins is coming off a major injury. She ranks second among all Division I players in scoring average with 26.8 points per game, while averaging career-highs in rebounds (7.6) and steals (3.8).

USC is off to a 4-1 start with its lone defeat coming against No. 1 ranked South Carolina on Nov. 15.

articles.title: JJ Redick Rips Lakers, Luka Doncic & Walker Kessler Reacts After Win vs. Kings in NBA Cup
articles.summary: Following a slow start to their NBA Cup group play game against the Sacramento Kings on Friday, Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick ripped into his team to great effect.
articles.body:
Following a slow start to their NBA Cup group play game against the Sacramento Kings on Friday, Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick ripped into his team to great effect.

Trailing by eight at halftime, the Lakers outscored the Kings by six in the third quarter and by four in the fourth en route to a 106-104 home victory.

Redick admitted after the game that he had some choice words for his players at halftime, telling reporters , "I feel I did a decent job of regulating at halftime. They may have a differing opinion of that. Can't repeat every word I used. The main message was we've got to be tougher, we've got to bring a little bit of energy."

Superstar guard Luka Dončić, who led the Lakers with 25 points, had no problem with Redick's approach, telling reporters , "I mean he yells, but I'm used to it. Got us all fired up. Sometimes it's good to yell."

One of the main recipients of Redick's criticism at halftime was center Walker Kessler, who had only six points and one rebound at halftime.

Kessler told reporters he was deserving of the backlash, saying, "He lit me up a little bit, rightfully so. But it was constructive. He was like, 'I know you can do this. Do it.'"

"I wasn't playing physical," Kessler continued. "I wasn't going up to dunk the ball. I was missing some more touches around the rim. And then defensively, being undisciplined. Jumping at stuff I don't need to jump at. He definitely lit into me. It was good. I needed it. That's what makes a good coach. Knowing when guys need that and when guys don't."

Whatever Redick said, it seemed to work, as Kessler was much better in the second half and finished the contest with 15 points, seven boards, three blocks and two assists.

While the Lakers did not play their best basketball Friday, it was a big win nonetheless coming off a disappointing 109-97 loss to the Utah Jazz on Wednesday.

That loss to Utah ended a nine-game winning streak, but L.A. now has a chance to start a new winning streak after outlasting the Kings.

A rematch with the Jazz is on tap Monday for a Lakers team that leads the Western Conference with a 14-3 record.

articles.title: Udoka Rips 'Mentally Fragile' Rockets After Kevin Durant, Houston Lose to Jokic, Nuggets in NBA Cup
articles.summary: Houston Rockets head coach Ime Udoka was not happy with his team's performance in a loss to the Denver Nuggets on Friday, calling them "mentally fragile."
articles.body:
Houston Rockets head coach Ime Udoka was not happy with his team's performance in a loss to the Denver Nuggets on Friday, calling them "mentally fragile."

The Rockets fell 133-124 to Denver in an NBA Cup group play game, and they had no answers defensively for the Nuggets, allowing seven different players to score in double figures.

Udoka told reporters , "They had four 30-point quarters. ... You're not going to win anything, and that just shows a lack of effort, attention to detail or fight on that end. And so, doesn't really matter what we did offensively. Play that poorly, you're not going to win any games."

Denver outscored Houston by 12 points in the fourth quarter, led by three-time NBA MVP Nikola Jokic, who led the Nuggets with 26 points to go along with 11 assists and seven rebounds.

Udoka said the Rockets showed "no effort or any attention to detail on the defensive end at all."

As a team, Denver shot a sizzling 55 percent from the field and 43 percent from three-point range, and every starter finished with at least 14 points.

The Rockets played well offensively in their own right, shooting 55 percent from the floor, but they only shot 33 percent from long range, which may have been the difference.

Four of Houston's five starters scored over 20 points, led by center Alperen Şengün and his 28.

The Rockets entered Friday's game having won five of their previous six games, and even with the loss, their 12-5 record has them fourth in the Western Conference.

Denver is only seventh with a 9-5 mark, but the Nuggets have now won four of their past five games following an uneven start to the season.

Udoka will look to get his Rockets team back on track Monday when they host the Los Angeles Clippers, which starts a five-game homestand.

articles.title: Watch LeBron's New Golf Video of '2v2 Shamble Rematch' amid 76ers' Season
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James posted video of his YouTube golf channel competing in a two-on-two shamble at Bandon Trails Golf Course in Bandon, Oregon.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James posted video of his YouTube golf channel competing in a two-on-two shamble at Bandon Trails Golf Course in Bandon, Oregon.

The USGA defines a shamble as follows: "In a shamble format, members of the team each hit a tee shot and select the best drive. From there, each player plays their own ball and the lowest score is the team score for the hole."

James and his partner, Randy Mims faced off against Lynn Merritt and David Creech over all 18 holes. It was a tough day for the James-Mims team, as it lost by eight holes.

Of course, James is a new golfer who recently picked up the sport a few years ago, so the loss is nothing to be ashamed of whatsoever as he learns the ins and outs of the game.

James was in Oregon last August during his annual trip to Nike World Headquarters. This year marked the release of the Nike LeBron 24.

James found some time for golf along the way. He nearly got a hole-in-one at The Preserve at Bandon Dunes during this trip.

Perhaps he'll get the elusive hole-in-one down the road. In the meantime, James and the 76ers lead the Eastern Conference with a 13-3 record.

articles.title: Early All-NBA Teams Predictions: Which 15 Stars Make The Cut After One Month?
articles.summary: One month into the 2026-27 NBA season, the All-NBA race is already getting fun. Here’s our early look at the 15 players who make the cut.
articles.body:
One month of NBA basketball is already giving us a lot to talk about when it comes to the All-NBA Teams, especially with how some of the best players in the league have started the 2026-27 season.

We've seen some crazy scoring numbers, teams winning a lot more games than expected, and even players who weren't considered All-NBA candidates before the season now getting into the conversation.

And picking the 15 best players has already become a little difficult, because not everyone putting up huge numbers is actually winning games. The Lakers and Spurs are fighting for the best record in the Western Conference, while the 76ers are sitting at the top of the East, and some of the NBA's best scorers are still trying to get their teams into playoff position.

So, how much should we reward winning when the individual numbers are so close? And what should we do with players who are playing incredible basketball but have already missed several games , like Anthony Edwards or Tyrese Haliburton?

For this first All-NBA exercise of the season, we're looking at individual numbers, team records, conference standings, and how much each player has helped his team so far. We're also leaving out players who've appeared in fewer than 11 games, because four or five great performances shouldn't be enough to get an All-NBA spot after the first 15 or 16 games.

With all that said, here are our early First, Second, and Third All-NBA Teams for the 2026-27 NBA season.

It's pretty wild that Ty Jerome has made this list, but his first 11 games have been too good to pass on. He's at 25.4 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 5.3 assists per game, shooting 48.5% from the field, 35.9% from three, and 90.2% at the line. His 45-point game against the Jazz wasn't just one random night, either, because he's scored at least 20 points in seven appearances. The Grizzlies have let him run their offense, and he's been taking advantage of those extra shots without turning into an inefficient scorer.

More importantly, Memphis is 12-4, third in the Western Conference, and has won five straight games. The latest was a 126-98 win over the Warriors on Thursday, so we're talking about production that has helped a team win, not just a surprise scoring average. Jerome has missed time with a right hip injury and only just reaches our 11-game requirement, which keeps him on the Third Team instead of higher. If he stays available and the Grizzlies stay near the top, he'll have a very strong case to move up.

For a second-year player, Cooper Flagg is doing almost everything the Mavericks ask him to do. His 24.2 points, 6.6 rebounds, 6.4 assists, and 2.1 steals per game would be impressive for an established All-Star, never mind someone who's only 20. He's shooting 48.5% from the field, creating shots against defenders who know he's Dallas' main option, and still finding teammates instead of forcing every shot. The passing and steals are why I'd keep him in this group even when some other forwards are scoring at a similar level.

The Mavericks are only 8-7 and ninth in the West, so there's an obvious reason not to put Flagg on the Second Team yet. He's also at 29.9% from three, and defenses are still comfortable giving him some space outside. That limits how much Dallas can do offensively when its other shooters aren't making shots. But Flagg's impact goes beyond his scoring, and it's difficult to leave out a player near 24 points, seven rebounds, six assists, and two steals. He needs more wins to climb, not much more individual production.

I had Deni Avdija outside the All-NBA conversation before the season, and now it's difficult to explain why he shouldn't be here. He's producing 24.2 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 6.1 assists in 13 games, with 50.7% shooting from the field and 38.6% from three. That's a strong combination for a forward, especially because Portland can use him as a scorer or let him handle the ball and create for others. He's not just standing on the perimeter waiting for open shots, and his improved shooting makes his drives much harder to defend.

The Trail Blazers are 10-5 and sixth in the West after Thursday's 124-114 win over the Bucks. That record gives Avdija an advantage over several players with similar averages on losing teams, and it's why I wouldn't call his season just a hot start. Portland is beating teams while giving him major offensive responsibility. He's appeared in 13 games, so staying healthy will be important, but right now the combination of 24 points, six assists, efficient shooting, and a top-six conference position gives him a deserved spot.

Jalen Brunson isn't scoring 35 every night, but the Knicks haven't needed him to do that after a very rough start. He's at 26.6 points and 5.9 assists per game, with 2.9 rebounds and only 1.8 turnovers, and that last number is especially good for a guard who handles the ball so much. Brunson is still the player New York trusts when the offense slows down, and his ability to get a decent shot late in the clock keeps the Knicks in tough games usually.

New York has climbed to 9-6, sixth in the East, and has won three straight games. Brunson scored 21 points and added seven assists in Thursday's 102-99 victory over the Timberwolves, which wasn't a huge scoring performance but helped the Knicks make progress in the East again. There are other guards with slightly better averages, yet I think his efficiency as a decision-maker and the recent winning streak deserve credit. If the Knicks get back toward the top three in the East, he'll be in a much better position for a Second Team spot.

Franz Wagner is probably the toughest player to keep on the Third Team because his recent stretch has been incredible. On Friday, he scored 35 points with five rebounds and seven assists against the Nets, then hit the game-winning jumper with 2.4 seconds left in a 113-111 win. His season averages are now 25.1 points, 6.8 rebounds, and 8.4 assists, which is a ridiculous passing number for a forward. Orlando has been using him as their No. 1 guy with Paolo Banchero sidelined, and he's responded amazingly.

But the Magic are still 7-8 and eighth in the Eastern Conference, and that record can't be ignored. They have won four of their last five games, with Franz posting 30.8 PPG, but their early losses still separate Wagner from some players on much better teams. I'd actually have no problem moving him into the Second Team if Orlando gets above .500 and he keeps putting up eight assists a game. For now, the individual case is excellent, while the team results are a little behind those of the other candidates.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Oklahoma City Thunder

Jamal Murray has given the Nuggets a scoring option they can trust every night, and his shooting numbers are some of the best in the league. He's putting up 24.9 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 5.8 assists, hitting 50.2% from the field and 46.3% from three. That's more than enough for a Denver team that was actually struggling to start the year. Murray has already scored 42 points in a game this season, and his outside shooting means defenders can't keep helping off him when Jokic gets the ball inside.

The Nuggets improved to 9-5 and seventh in the West after beating the Rockets 133-124 on Friday. Murray finished with 14 points and seven assists, and it was a useful reminder that he doesn't need a 30-point game whenever Denver wins. Still, seventh place isn't enough to give two Nuggets players automatic All-NBA Team consideration, especially with other contenders owning better records. Murray is having an All-NBA season because he's scoring efficiently, creating for teammates, and helping Denver win, but the team needs to keep climbing if he wants a higher spot.

The 76ers have started 13-3, the best record in the East, and Tyrese Maxey is a huge reason why. He's scoring 26.5 points per game with 3.3 rebounds and 5.8 assists, while shooting 50.0% from the field and 38.0% from three. He's taking almost 18 shots per game and still making half of them, so Philadelphia is getting high-level scoring without needing to sacrifice efficiency. Maxey can score off the dribble, hit outside shots, and take pressure away from the rest of the stars when the game asks for it.

Philadelphia has won four straight games, and Maxey has stayed consistent throughout its excellent start. For me, his First Team argument is stronger than some people might think, because leading the East while scoring more than 26 points efficiently should count for a lot. The problem is the competition above him: Doncic is scoring almost 11 more points per game, while players like Wembanyama and Giannis are also dominating defensively or on the glass. Maxey is right there, though, and another month at 13-3 pace could change the order.

Cade Cunningham has been running one of the better teams in the East, and that's enough to put him above several guards with similar scoring numbers. He's averaging 25.6 points, 5.1 rebounds, 7.9 assists, and 1.4 steals for the Pistons, who are 10-5 and third in the conference. I especially like the passing, because Detroit isn't asking him to score on every trip. He has to find teammates, control the pace, and still be the first player defenses worry about. Almost eight assists while scoring more than 25 points is a difficult combination to stop.

Friday wasn't a great night for Detroit, which lost 105-102 to the Raptors, but Cunningham still finished with 23 points, five rebounds, and nine assists. The Pistons also beat the Spurs 105-93 earlier in the week, showing they can compete with one of the best teams in the West. I wouldn't move Cade down over one loss, especially when Detroit has a better record than the Knicks and Magic. The next step is staying near the top of the East as the schedule gets tougher. If the Pistons do that, he could end up competing with Maxey for a First Team place.

Alperen Sengun gave us one of Friday's best individual performances, even though the Rockets lost to the Nuggets. He posted 28 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists on 9-for-16 shooting against Nikola Jokic , and Houston needed everything he created to stay in the game. For the season, Sengun is at 22.1 points, 9.3 rebounds, and 7.0 assists on 54.7% shooting. Those aren't typical center numbers, especially the assists, because he's become the player the Rockets use to organize a lot of their schemes.

Houston is 12-5 and fourth in the West, so his production is coming with strong team results as well. Kevin Durant is still there, but Sengun is leading the Rockets in points, rebounds, and assists, which says plenty about how much responsibility he's carrying. I think his passing is the difference between him and several other big men in the All-NBA conversation. He can score against single coverage, find open shooters when opponents send help, and grab close to 10 rebounds a night. Friday's loss hurts the record, but it doesn't really weaken his individual case.

If this were based on scoring alone, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander would be an easy First Team pick. He's at 31.7 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 4.4 assists in 16 games, and he just scored 40 against the Pelicans on Friday. OKC needed that performance to win 126-120 after trailing in the fourth quarter, and Shai took over when the Thunder were in danger of losing another close game. His ability to get to his spots and score without needing many three-pointers is still one of the biggest problems for opposing defenses.

The Thunder are 10-6 and eighth in the West, though, and they've won only two of their last six games. That's the reason he's on the Second Team instead of the First, not because he's stopped playing like a superstar. It's a tough call when someone is scoring more than 31 points per night, but with OKC missing three starters for a long stretch of the season, the race becomes uphill. Shai could move back up very quickly if the Thunder start winning more consistently. Right now, his individual numbers are ahead of the team results.

Jayson Tatum has turned into Boston's undisputed main guy, and the Celtics have benefited from it. He's averaging 26.4 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 6.8 assists, giving Boston scoring while also an increased playmaking ability. Tatum still gets his own shots, but he's also finding open teammates when defenses load up on him, which has been important for a team that expects to compete for the East's top seed. Almost seven assists alongside 26 points is a strong offensive season even before considering his defense.

Boston is 11-4 and second in the East, although it has lost two straight games. Tatum recorded 24 points, eight rebounds, and three assists in Wednesday's 105-101 loss to the Nuggets, and I think the Celtics need to end this small skid before their position starts hurting his case. It's close between him, Maxey, and Shai for this spot. I'm choosing Tatum because of his all-around production and Boston's record, but he probably has the least room for error among my First Team picks. A few more losses could easily change the decision.

Nikola Jokic is still putting up numbers that almost nobody else can match, even with Jamal scoring more for Denver this season. He's averaging 24.2 points, 10.4 rebounds, and 9.1 assists on 52.6% shooting, and the Nuggets continue to run a huge part of their offense through him, even with the early-season struggles . The scoring is lower than in some previous years, while his three-point percentage is down to 30.0%, but he's still close to averaging a triple-double. Opponents can't focus only on stopping Jokic in the paint because he'll find Murray or another teammate if they leave someone open.

Denver moved to 9-5 after Friday's 133-124 win over Houston , with Jokic delivering 26 points, seven rebounds, and 11 assists. He scored 24 points after halftime, which helped the Nuggets pull away despite Sengun's triple-double. Seventh place in the West isn't where Denver wants to be, so I understand the argument for lowering him and rewarding someone on a better team. But I still have Jokic on the First Team because 24 points, 10 rebounds, and nine assists are incredible numbers, and he's the main reason the Nuggets can compete against almost anyone.

Since joining the Heat , Giannis Antetokounmpo has given Miami an interior scorer and rebounder who can completely change games. He's posting 28.2 points, 12.6 rebounds, 5.5 assists, and 1.3 blocks while shooting 60.2% from the field. That's the kind of production we'd expect from him at his best, and there's little opponents can do when he's attacking the rim and getting to the line. Miami has also found ways to use his passing, which helps the offense when opponents put several defenders in his path.

The Heat are 9-6 and fifth in the East, but they've won six straight games, so the current direction is much better than the overall record suggests. Giannis nearly had a triple-double against his former Bucks on Wednesday , finishing with 27 points, 14 rebounds, and nine assists in a 137-130 win. It's fair to question giving a First Team spot to someone whose team is only fifth, especially when Maxey's 76ers are 13-3. But for me, 28 points and almost 13 boards on better than 60.0% shooting, plus Miami's winning streak, are enough to keep Giannis here.

Victor Wembanyama has been the best defensive force among the players on this list, and his offense is now at an MVP level too. He's putting up 28.6 points, 11.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists, and 3.9 blocks while shooting 52.8% from the field. Almost four blocks per game changes how teams attack the paint, because opponents have to think twice before taking shots near him. And San Antonio is getting all of that while he plays around 30 minutes a night, meaning his numbers could be even higher if the Spurs needed to use him more.

The Spurs are 13-3, second in the West, and only half a game behind the Lakers after beating the Clippers 124-112 on Thursday. They've also started 7-0 on the road, so this isn't a team winning only at home. I think Wembanyama has one of the strongest MVP cases because both sides of his game are affecting wins. He's giving the Spurs almost 29 points and 12 rebounds while protecting the rim at an elite level, so if he keeps producing like this, he could be fighting for MVP and Defensive Player of the Year at the same time.

And finally, Luka Doncic is the easiest First Team choice after one month. The Lakers are 14-3, first in the West, and he's leading the NBA with 37.2 points per game, adding 6.8 rebounds, 7.7 assists, and 1.9 steals. That's almost 37 points and eight assists for the team with the conference's best record, which is a difficult argument for anyone else to beat right now. He's shooting 46.8% from the field while taking more than 25 shots per game, and even when defenders try to take away his scoring, he can create open looks for teammates.

Friday wasn't one of his huge scoring nights, but the Lakers still beat the Kings 106-104 , with Doncic finishing on 25 points, four rebounds, and eight assists. Quentin Grimes hit a big three-pointer late, and LA picked up its 10th win in 11 games. I think that record is what separates Luka from Shai in this early race, because both can score at an incredible level, but the Lakers are winning much more often right now. Wembanyama and Giannis have arguments based on defense and rebounding, and Jokic remains the best mind in basketball. Still, 37.2 points and a 14-3 record make Doncic my top All-NBA pick today.
